_about.what: Verification status of each intervention in the county-bundle catalog (D.catalog). The page shows a dollar or $-per-$1 figure only for verified and partially_verified items; unverified items are listed by name only.

status.verified: effect size and cost both confirmed against a source fetched in the audit
status.partially_verified: one side confirmed (or, for items with no dollar effect, the cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched)
status.unverified: neither confirmed, source not found, not reproducible, or labelled an unchecked AI research pass in the catalog

effect.checked: the effect size used was found in the cited source's text
effect.unchecked: the study exists or is named, but the number used was not confirmed (or the item estimates no dollar effect)
effect.misapplied: the number is real but applied outside the conditions the study measured
effect.not_found: the cited study or its data could not be found

cost.checked: the unit cost was found in a fetched document
cost.unchecked: the cost cites a document that was not re-fetched, or has no source

street_trees.evidence: City Pretty local hedonic (3,386 Westside sales): no regression code or sales data in repo or git history; irreproducible. Shipped to 637 non-LA counties as "local sales estimate".
street_trees.notes: Unverified: the catalog's grade-A effect comes from a 'City Pretty local hedonic' regression (3,386 Westside sales, 2022-24) whose code and sales data are not in the repository or its git history, so it cannot be reproduced. Confirmed street-tree studies exist in research/effects.csv (Donovan & Butry 2010; Sander, Polasky & Haight 2010) but the model does not use them yet. The same 0.24% was shipped to 637 non-LA counties labelled 'local sales estimate'. Cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched (most LA agency sites return 403 from the audit machine).

affordable_housing.evidence: Diamond & McQuade abstract confirms +6.5%/-2.5% (OpenAlex). MISAPPLIED: study +6.5% is for tracts with median income under ~$26k; engine applies it below LA median $93,240
affordable_housing.notes: Diamond & McQuade's +6.5% (confirmed in their abstract) is for low-income neighborhoods; the catalog's citation gives the cut-off as median income under ~$26k (the abstract does not state the figure), and -2.5% in higher-income areas. The original build applied +6.5% wherever income was below LA's median ($93,240): misapplied. The page now shows this estimate only where the block group's median household income is below $26,000. Cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched (most LA agency sites return 403 from the audit machine).
